messages.body_plain:
I have a question, which may be simple, if anyone can help me that would be great!

inNode46 >  founder (j) > Z->Z,A > clade dispersal to A

but in my graphic, this is the event pointed (sending the image in the attachment)

ZE > ZE, A

Which event should I consider for the species in question? did they originate in Z or in ZE?

messages.subject: Re: [BioGeoBEARS] Clado events table x model graphic question
messages.subject_clean: [BioGeoBEARS] Clado events table x model graphic question
messages.body_plain:
Hi!

This is probably the distinction between:

(1) the standard "most probable range at each node/corner" plot -- this is produced by the default Maximum Likelihood analysis of each model. This analysis reports the ancestral range probabilities, for each possible range at each node/corner (producing the pie charts) and then the single most-probable range is reported in the plot like the one you've pasted in.  This is giving ancestral range probabilities, which is not technically a history of specific dispersal events, although the "reading events by eye" strategy will.

(2) the events tables come from running Biogeographical Stochastic Mapping (BSM). If you average 100+ BSMs -- each of which has an exact event history, and exact ancestral ranges, *for that specific sampled/simulated BSM* -- you will converge on (1), above.

So, probably, you are looking at a BSM events table which had an event history for that node, which simulated an ancestral range slightly different than the most-probable range reported by the ML analysis.

Dupin, Matzke et al., or phylowiki, explain the differences between these approaches -- cheers!

Cheers!
Nick

Hi Bert!

Hopefully, yes -- of course all of these methods and models have severe limitations, and so will new models that include extinction, sampling, and other processes usually ignored. But yeah, the criticisms in that paper were way off.  Hopefully, researchers will work to understand the assumptions & strengths/weaknesses of various methods/models, rather than following the whatever-the-latest-authority-says approach...

Cheers,
Nick

messages.subject: max_range_size Fatal Error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Nick and everyone,

I'm new to BioGeoBEARS and ancestral area reconstruction (ancestral range estimation, I did my research) in general. I'm trying to analyse a small dataset of 16 species on 10 different areas. As the analysis takes ages to run with that many areas, I would like to set the max_range_size to 3 or 4 but it gives me this error message when I check the parameters with check_BioGeoBEARS_run(BioGeoBEARS_run_object) :

FATAL ERROR in inputs: max_tipsize=6 > inputs$max_range_size=3

I understand that it's because one of my species have a present range of 6 areas but I don't get why it's a problem to constrain the reconstruction. I'm working on bryophytes, a large geographic range is almost the rule. Is there any way to run the analysis without decreasing the number of areas?

Very best,
Sébastien
